title: Mastering Python For Loops
audience: Beginner programmers in Indian colleges writing their first Python loops
lesson_objective: After watching, the learner can write a for loop over range and predict each line it prints.
short_description: A visual introduction to Python for loops: iteration, range start and stop rules, and the loop body.

voice_profile.persona: Patient instructor explaining at a whiteboard
voice_profile.modulation: Slow slightly while tracing iterations; emphasize the range rule
voice_profile.provider_notes: gTTS with tld co.in. Express rhythm through punctuation and short sentences; gTTS has no pitch or emotion controls.

scenes.title: Meet the For Loop
scenes.purpose: Set the goal: repeat work over a sequence without copying code.
scenes.voiceover: Welcome to AI Sankalp. Today we will learn the Python for loop. By the end, you will be able to repeat an action for every item in a sequence, and predict exactly what the loop prints.

voice_delivery.modulation: Lift gently on the lesson promise

animation_notes: Reveal the title, then the three learning verbs.
scenes.transition: Title fades into the motivation cards.

scenes.title: Why Not Copy and Paste?
scenes.purpose: Show why repetition needs a loop.
scenes.voiceover: Suppose you want to print the squares of the numbers one to five. You could write five print statements. But what if you need one hundred numbers? Copying code is slow and easy to get wrong. A loop writes the action once and repeats it for you.

voice_delivery.modulation: Slow down on the one hundred numbers question

animation_notes: Stack five repeated print cards, then collapse them into one loop card.
scenes.transition: Loop card moves into the explanation.

scenes.title: How One Iteration Works
scenes.purpose: Build the mental model of a single pass.
scenes.voiceover: A for loop walks through a sequence one item at a time. Python takes the first item and stores it in the loop variable. Then it runs the indented body. When the body finishes, Python moves to the next item and repeats. When there are no items left, the loop ends.

voice_delivery.modulation: Pause briefly after each stage of the cycle

animation_notes: Reveal the iteration cycle as a four-step flow, highlighting each step as it is named.
scenes.transition: Flow shrinks beside the range explanation.

scenes.title: Counting With range
scenes.purpose: Explain range start and stop rules.
scenes.voiceover: To count, we often loop over range. Range of one comma six produces the numbers one, two, three, four, and five. The start value is included, but the stop value is excluded. That is why six never appears.
animation_notes: Show range(1, 6) and reveal the five produced numbers; cross out 6.
scenes.transition: Number strip slides under the code panel.

scenes.title: Read the Program
scenes.purpose: Connect the loop syntax to its behavior.
scenes.voiceover: Here is the complete program. The first line says: for number in range one comma six, followed by a colon. The two indented lines form the loop body. The body computes the square of number, and then prints the number and its square. Indentation tells Python which lines belong to the loop.
animation_notes: Reveal the code and highlight the header, the square line, and the print line in order.
scenes.transition: Code panel stays as the trace begins.

scenes.title: Trace Every Pass
scenes.purpose: Trace the loop variable and the output.
scenes.voiceover: Let us trace it. First, number is one, so the program prints one and one. Next, number is two, and it prints two and four. Then three and nine. Then four and sixteen. Finally five and twenty five. Range has no more numbers, so the loop stops.
animation_notes: Move a marker across the numbers and append each output row.
scenes.transition: Output table fades as the mistake appears.

scenes.title: The Indentation Mistake
scenes.purpose: Show how missing indentation breaks the loop body.
scenes.voiceover: A common mistake is forgetting to indent the body. If the print line is not indented, Python raises an IndentationError, because the loop header expects an indented block. Always indent the body by four spaces.

voice_delivery.modulation: Slightly firmer on the error name

animation_notes: Show the unindented code with an error badge, then fix the indentation.

scenes.title: Your Turn
scenes.voiceover: Your turn. What does for n in range two comma five, print n, display? Pause and predict. The answer is two, three, and four, because the stop value five is excluded.

voice_delivery.modulation: Leave a real pause after the question

animation_notes: Show the question, hold for three seconds, then reveal the answer.
scenes.transition: Answer card fades into the recap.

scenes.title: What You Learned
scenes.voiceover: Let us recap. A for loop processes one sequence item at a time. The loop variable changes on every iteration. Range includes its start and excludes its stop. And indented statements form the loop body.

voice_delivery.modulation: Settle the pace for the closing line

animation_notes: Reveal four recap cards in narration order.
scenes.transition: Recap cards fade into the closing line.

scenes.title: Keep Building
scenes.purpose: Close the lesson and point to the next topic.
scenes.voiceover: Thank you for learning with AI Sankalp. Next, try while loops. Keep learning, and keep building.

voice_delivery.modulation: Settle gently on the closing line

animation_notes: Reveal the closing line and a small next-step label.

code_examples.purpose: Loop over range(1, 6) and print each number with its square.
explanation_steps: On each pass, number holds the current value.
The body computes number * number and stores it in square.
print outputs the number and its square on one line.
beginner_mistakes: Expecting range(1, 6) to include 6; the stop value is excluded.
Forgetting to indent the body, which raises IndentationError.
Forgetting the colon at the end of the for header.
code_examples.practice_variation: Change the loop to range(2, 5) and predict the printed numbers.
